1. Core Clinical Tension: A 31-year-old female presents with two weeks of high fevers, dramatic leukemoid reaction (WBC 36.18 × 10^9/L), extensive necrotic lymphadenopathy, facial plaques, and papulonodular skin lesions unresponsive to broad-spectrum oral antibiotics. The presentation mimics lymphoma, Sweet syndrome, or systemic lupus erythematosus, obscuring lepromatous disease complicated by an acute Type 2 immune reaction (erythema nodosum leprosum).
2. Admission Breakpoint: The breakpoint occurs following emergency admission, systemic staging computed tomography demonstrating necrotic lymphadenopathy, and autoimmune serologies, strictly prior to targeted peripheral nerve palpation and skin biopsy.
3. Differential Distinctions: Tumid lupus erythematosus presents with indurated facial plaques, but typically demonstrates positive ANA/dsDNA or hypocomplementemia. Sweet syndrome and lymphoproliferative disorders cause severe neutrophilic leukocytosis, high fevers, and cutaneous plaques, but lack pathognomonic peripheral nerve thickening and acid-fast bacillary burden.
case_prompt:
A 31-year-old Filipino female domestic worker presented to the emergency department with a two-week history of persistent high-grade fevers and painful bilateral groin swellings that caused significant difficulty ambulating. She had been evaluated twice in primary care and prescribed sequential courses of oral amoxicillin-clavulanate (one week) and moxifloxacin (five days) without clinical improvement. Ten days into the illness, an eruption appeared over her hands and lower extremities, accompanied by circumoral numbness without dyspnea or dysphagia. Over the subsequent four days, the eruption spread to involve her face and ears, alongside newly tender swellings in both axillae.

On physical examination, her temperature was 39.2°C (102.6°F), heart rate 120 beats per minute, and blood pressure 130/80 mmHg. Dermatologic examination revealed an erythematous papulonodular eruption distributed across the extensor surfaces of the upper and lower extremities, and multiple indurated plaques over the nasal bridge, forehead, outer maxillary area, pinnae, and earlobes. Bilateral ankle edema was present. Palpation revealed tender, enlarged, and matted cervical, axillary, and inguinal lymphadenopathy. General examination of other organ systems was unremarkable.

Laboratory studies demonstrated marked leukocytosis of 36.18 × 10^9/L, an erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) of 80 mm/h, and a C-reactive protein (CRP) level of 159 mg/L. Serum alkaline phosphatase was elevated at 316 IU/L with normal transaminases, and serum albumin was 34 g/L. Serologic evaluation for HIV, antinuclear antibodies (ANA), double-stranded DNA antibodies, and complement components C3 and C4 was normal. A contrast CT scan of the neck, thorax, abdomen, and pelvis showed no intra-abdominal or hepatobiliary focus, but confirmed multiple enlarged and necrotic lymph nodes within the axillary and inguinal chains.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Tumid lupus erythematosus or systemic connective tissue disease
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to indurated erythematous facial plaques, peripheral edema, and constitutional symptoms, but excluded by negative antinuclear antibodies, negative double-stranded DNA antibodies, and normal serum complement (C3, C4) concentrations.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The differential diagnoses considered included tumid lupus erythematosus, sarcoidosis, cutaneous amyloidosis, lymphoproliferative disease, Sweet syndrome, and Hansen disease. ... HIV testing, antinuclear antibody, C3, C4, and double-stranded DNA levels were normal.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered given high fevers, dramatic leukemoid leukocytosis (36.18 x 10^9/L), extensive necrotic lymphadenopathy on CT, and an acute inflammatory dermatosis, but ruled out when biopsy demonstrated foamy histiocytic infiltration with perineural inflammation rather than malignant lymphoma or aseptic neutrophilic dermatosis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The differential diagnoses considered included tumid lupus erythematosus, sarcoidosis, cutaneous amyloidosis, lymphoproliferative disease, Sweet syndrome, and Hansen disease. ... Routine investigations revealed leukocytosis of 36.18 x 109/L, an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 80 mm/h and a C-reactive protein level of 159 mg/L.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Physical palpation demonstrating bilaterally thickened greater auricular and lateral peroneal nerves, followed by a punch skin biopsy revealing a diffuse dermal and subcutaneous infiltrate containing foamy macrophages with neurovascular tropism and abundant acid-fast bacilli on Fite and Ziehl-Neelsen stains, confirmed lepromatous leprosy with erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL).
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Closer examination revealed bilaterally thickened greater auricular nerves and lateral peroneal nerves, which further raised the suspicion of leprosy. ... Skin biopsy was performed and histological examination showed a diffuse inflammatory infiltrate within the dermis and subcutaneous tissue, sparing the epidermis. The inflammatory infiltrate was composed of lymphocytes, histiocytes, foamy macrophages, and neutrophils. Some of the inflammation involved the nerves and adnexal structures. Large numbers of acid-fast bacilli were identified on Fite and Ziehl-Neelsen stains. These features are consistent with the diagnosis of lepromatous leprosy with erythema nodosum leprosum.

editor_comments: This case highlights an atypical presentation of lepromatous leprosy with extensive necrotizing lymphadenitis and erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL) masquerading as lymphoma or Sweet syndrome with marked leukocytosis in a non-endemic urban setting.
